blind_editorial_judgments: HUMAN_ENDPOINT is the editorial authority and remains the preferred passage regardless of detector results.
All four synthetic probes preserve the same substantive imbalance claim and leave the surrounding claims, agency, chronology, attribution, and examples unchanged.
P_A0B0 is plain and clear, though slightly more repetitive and abstract than HUMAN_ENDPOINT.
P_A0B1 and P_A1B0 are grammatical and intelligible but stylistically less balanced; they are diagnostic probes, not publication candidates.
P_A1B1 is coherent but more schematic and hyperbolic than HUMAN_ENDPOINT.
No Pangram result will justify replacing HUMAN_ENDPOINT with a less natural synthetic realization.

factors.description: Realization of the high-romantic-love half of the imbalance claim.

factors.description: Realization of the low-selfless-love half of the same imbalance claim.

factors.name: Selfless-clause realization

objective: Determine whether the prior regression requires the joint matched form “the romantic part is … and the selfless part is …,” is driven by either clause alone, or fails to transfer to the Human endpoint boundary. The experiment tests the A×B interaction without subdividing into individual words.

probes.controlled_variable: Endpoint anchor; not part of the factorial.
probes.text:
Then there’s romantic love: I want you. I want your attention, your body, your specialness, your life intertwined with mine. There’s nothing fake or shameful about that. Romantic love is one of the most powerful things we get. But it is, by its nature, about what I want from one particular person.

A good relationship can hold both. Trouble starts when the romantic part is enormous and the selfless part is mostly decorative. Then I may adore how you make me feel, what you give me, even who I get to be beside you — while caring much less about what is actually best for you.

probes.controlled_variable: Editorial-authority anchor; not part of the factorial.
probes.text:
Then we use the same word for romantic love: I want you. I want your attention and your body. I want to be special to you, and I want our lives tangled up together. I don’t think there’s anything fake or shameful about this. Romantic love is one of the most powerful feelings we get. Here I’m wanting something from one particular person.

A good relationship can have both kinds of love at once. The trouble is when there’s a whole lot of I want you and hardly any I want you to be happy. I can adore how you make me feel and what you give me. I can even adore who I get to be with you, while caring a lot less about what’s actually best for you.

stop_rule: After harness-scheduled repeats, bind the result and stop this local branch: if only P_A1B1 regresses, record a matched two-clause interaction; if a mixed cell follows P_A1B1, record the corresponding clause-level realization as sufficient in this boundary; if the factorial contrasts are null, record failure to transfer onto the Human-endpoint boundary. Do not subdivide these clauses into token-level tests. A follow-up is warranted only for a stable divergence between the two mixed cells that the preregistered contrasts cannot resolve.
summary: Run a complete-passage 2×2 factorial that decomposes the previously detector-sensitive matched-part imbalance sentence into its romantic and selfless clause realizations. This supplies the missing opposite mixed cell while keeping the Human endpoint’s surrounding passage fixed.
why_high_information: The design fills the decisive missing opposite mixed cell and places all four combinations on one fixed, editorially preferred complete-passage boundary. It distinguishes a genuinely joint matched-part interaction from either clause acting alone or from boundary-local non-replication, while avoiding magic-word inference and token hunting.
